verdict_reason: Wave 2 added 93 MUST rules and 84 ranked failure modes in seven freshly opened families, so it has not converged. Seven of the fourteen artifact families have no consolidation yet: GO-LANG, GO-API, GO-NET, GO-SEC, GO-REL, GO-OBS and BZL-GO. Three of those carry P0 rows: M-A-10/14, M-D-01/02/17 and M-H-01/03/07. The fleet golangci config the drafters would copy verbatim (GO-GATE-09) enables the std-error-handling preset, which GO-ERR-09 forbids as a MUST. Several load-bearing questions can be answered now by a fixture run or a source read: errorlint's MUST admission rests on a 0/15 sample, the GO-IO-14 pgid sweep has not been checked for reuse safety, GO-CLI-06's skeleton edge cases are untested, and the SDK surface is undecided.

frame_corrections: go mod init on 1.27.1 writes `go 1.27.1`: the 1.26.0 N-1 default was reverted in 1.26.1 (golang/go#77653, #77860). This overturns the premise of map conflict 12 and M-L-03 (go-modules.md conflict 6, GO-MOD-01).

golangci-lint v2 has no default exclusions, so a bare `defer resp.Body.Close()` is an errcheck finding unless it is exempted with exclude-functions (io.ReadCloser).Close (GO-ERR-08/09). The map's 'Explicitly not a defect' entry for it is wrong.
The omitzero go fix fixer declines its behaviour-changing rewrite by default (GO-GATE-03). Map M3's 'changes JSON output' was overstated.
noctx covers os/exec and the net family at golangci-lint 2.14.0. Map row M-G-08's 'to be confirmed' is answered yes (GO-CONC-03).
vet waitgroup and hostport fire regardless of the module's go line once the toolchain is >=1.25 (go-gates.md C-10).
testinggoroutine is not in go test's vet subset (go1.27.1:src/cmd/go/internal/test/test.go:684). stdversion joined that subset only in 1.27.
Stdlib API availability is not gated by the go line: errors.AsType compiles under `go 1.25` on a 1.27 toolchain. Only vet stdversion catches it; staticcheck does not (GO-ERR-04).
After staticcheck 2026.2 disabled SA5011, nil-dereference detection needs govet enable-all (nilness). Bare go vet and golangci's default govet miss it (go-gates.md C-1).
cobra never calls os.Exit (spf13/cobra@adbc8813901b:command.go:1070-1073). Map row M-F-03's 'cobra default exit 1' describes the author's main, not cobra.
signal.NotifyContext's 1.26 cause is an unexported string with no signal accessor (go1.27.1:src/os/signal/signal.go:352-361). It is not a typed exit path (GO-CLI-08, GO-CONC-17).
errorlint errorf is on by default under golangci-lint 2.14.0. Map conflict 22's 'ships off' holds only for standalone go-errorlint.
archive/tar and archive/zip are permissive by default in 1.27.1. Only a godebug pin in a main module enables ErrInsecurePath (GO-IO-05).

tailscale does not layer staticcheck.conf under golangci's staticcheck (tailscale/tailscale@6b3a45f14ef6:.golangci.yml:9-15). Map conflict 20's evidence is corrected, and its rule now stands on go-gates.md C-3.
trivy enables the std-error-handling preset (aquasecurity/trivy@ae561f8cca36:.golangci.yaml:201), as do 13 of the 23 exemplar configs.
GODEBUG=execwait=2 panics the program. It is a CI and diagnosis switch, never a runtime default (go-io.md conflict 11).
contradictions_across_consolidations: 1. GO-GATE-09's config enables the std-error-handling preset (go-gates.md:180), which GO-ERR-09 forbids as a MUST; GO-ERR-09's own grep goes red on the fleet config. GO-ERR-09 keeps its text. GO-GATE-09's config drops the preset and adds errcheck exclude-functions [(io.ReadCloser).Close]. The gates/config-revision dive measures the errcheck volume change first.
2. GO-GATE-10 (uniq-by-line false, MUST) conflicts with GO-ERR-13's verification ('leave uniq-by-line at its default') and go-errors conflict 7. GO-GATE-10 keeps its text, and GO-ERR-13 cites it.

3. GO-ERR-13 wants gocritic 'at its defaults'; GO-GATE-15/18 allow gocritic only as disable-all plus enabled-checks, in the CLI overlay. GO-GATE-15/18 keep their text. exitAfterDefer matters only in func main, and libraries get revive deep-exit from the baseline.

4. GO-GATE-13's depguard list (6 entries) and GO-MOD-08's (12 entries on files $all) are both MUST on the same linter. GO-MOD-08 owns the list text. GO-GATE-09's config quotes it verbatim, and GO-GATE-13 becomes a citation row: its ID is kept and never renumbered.

5. GO-TEST's 'go-cmp is the only SDK test dependency' conflicts with GO-CONC-11's goleak MUST for the SDK. GO-CONC-11 keeps its text under the owner default (admit goleak), and GO-TEST's SDK commitment is reworded to name both. The observability dive tests a stdlib runtime.Stack diff that could reverse this.

6. Citation drift: go-concurrency, go-testing and go-modules cite GO-GATE-COMMANDS-01/02/04/05/08, which no consolidation defines (13 citations). The drafters map -01->GO-GATE-01, -02->GO-GATE-02, -04->GO-GATE-03, -08->GO-GATE-04 and -05->GO-MOD-03.

7. The per-family config fragments in go-concurrency, go-cli and go-errors restate YAML. The concurrency fragment's one-rule revive list would replace deep-exit if copied. GO-GATE-09 and GO-GATE-18 are the only config text; depth files cite linter names and never paste YAML.
8. GO-CLI-02's three-statement main with reraise conflicts with GO-ERR's `func main(){ os.Exit(run()) }` and map M-F-01's two-line main. GO-CLI-02 keeps its text.

9. GO-IO-01 and GO-CONC-03 are both MUST on noctx and both name exec.Command. GO-IO-01 keeps the os/exec text. GO-CONC-03 narrows to the net/http and net forms, and GO-NET cites GO-CONC-03 rather than adding a third row.

10. GO-CONC-17 has CLIs keep signal.NotifyContext for propagation, while GO-CLI-08 wires signal.Notify into WithCancelCause and ExecuteContext with no NotifyContext. GO-CLI-08 keeps the CLI wiring text; GO-CONC-17 keeps the SDK cause clause and points to GO-CLI-08.

11. GO-ERR-12's nilnil rule is SHOULD, but nilnil sits in the blocking baseline. There is no conflict under the house tiers: `//nolint:nilnil // <reason>` is the stated reason. The config gains GO-ERR-12's checked-types, which GO-GATE-09 lacks. The go-gates open question is closed.

12. GO-ERR-20's *TimeoutError and GO-CONC-17's exported ErrOcxTimeout cause represent one event twice. GO-ERR-20 keeps the type. The sentinel becomes TimeoutError's Is target, and the *TimeoutError value is the WithTimeoutCause cause (provisional; api/sdk-surface pins it with a contract test).

13. GO-CLI-01's exhaustive clause meets an SDK that mirrors the 0-86 table, while GO-GATE-18's overlay is CLI-only. The clause binds CLIs only until api/sdk-surface measures it; GO-GATE-18 keeps its text.

14. GO-GATE-01 runs go fix -diff and golangci once, but GO-MOD-16 tests libraries on [oldstable, stable], and the fixer and analyzer sets differ by toolchain (atomictypes needs 1.27). GO-GATE-01's text states it: steps 1-4, 7 and 8 run on the stable leg; steps 5-6 run on every matrix leg. GO-MOD-16 keeps its text.

15. GO-IO-06 and GO-CLI-07 rely on `GOOS=windows go vet ./...`, which GO-GATE-01's block lacks. GO-GATE-07's Windows and macOS legs satisfy it for the SDK and CLIs; libraries run GO-IO-06's command. Both keep their text.

16. Open questions answered by a sibling: go-testing Q2 (the usetesting context settings) is answered by go-gates C-6 (all hits are true-positive debt); go-concurrency Q2 (context linters with tests) by GO-GATE-09; go-io Q2 (gosec thresholds) by GO-GATE-14.
17. GO-TEST-12's use of execwait=2 and go-io conflict 11 are consistent: it is a CI and diagnosis switch, never a runtime rule. GO-TEST-12 keeps its text.
